title: Trump: DOGE physically blocks Democratic lawmakers from four federal agencies
description_short: Trump: DOGE physically blocks Democratic lawmakers from four federal agencies
description_medium: Trumpfile reports that lawmakers were blocked from entering USAID, Treasury, EPA and the Department of Education during the first week of February 2025. Its account names a security official at Education, while Axios independently confirms that lawmakers were denied entry to Treasury and USAID. Axios does not corroborate the Education or EPA incidents or establish that DOGE directed the access decisions.
description_long: In early February 2025, congressional Democrats attempted to visit federal agencies affected by the new Department of Government Efficiency. Trumpfile’s February 7 timeline says 30 to 40 lawmakers went to the Department of Education to seek a meeting with Acting Secretary Denise Carter and were stopped at the entrance by security official Jim Hairfield. The page also lists denied visits to USAID on Monday, Treasury on Tuesday and EPA on Thursday. Axios independently reported that lawmakers protesting DOGE’s access to Treasury payment systems were denied entry there, and that Democrats had been blocked from USAID the previous day. Its report does not cover the Department of Education or EPA incidents. The available reporting therefore supports specific access disputes but does not establish that DOGE itself physically blocked lawmakers at all four agencies, or identify an administration-wide instruction authorizing those denials. The security records, agency accounts and authority for each decision remain necessary to establish who ordered the restrictions and whether the incidents shared a common policy.
notes: The supplied timeline and Axios article corroborate denied access at some agencies, including Treasury and USAID, but not all four incidents or a shared directive. Records naming the decision-makers and authority for each denial are needed to support the broader claim.

title: Trump: LEAK: Elon Musk's DOGE infiltrates National Institutes of Health
description_short: Trump: LEAK: Elon Musk's DOGE infiltrates National Institutes of Health
description_medium: WIRED reports that four DOGE-affiliated employees were listed at NIH and that internal records placed three of them in the NIH Business System department, which supports finance, procurement, property management and grant tracking. The reporting identifies the system and staff, but does not establish each person’s exact permissions, what data they viewed or changed, or whether access was authorized under applicable rules.
description_long: WIRED reported in February 2025 that government records identified four DOGE-associated workers at the National Institutes of Health: Luke Farritor, Rachel Riley, Jeremy Lewin and Clark Minor. Internal documents reviewed by the outlet placed Farritor, Riley and Minor in the NIH Business System department. WIRED described that system as supporting the agency’s finance, budget, procurement, property management and grant-tracking functions, and quoted an NIH employee calling it the agency’s “wallet.” These records document agency placements and the sensitivity of the system, but do not by themselves show what each person could access or whether they opened, changed or exported specific data. The available reporting does not supply permission logs, system-owner approvals, audit records or the full NIH records needed to determine whether access was authorized and what functions DOGE personnel actually used. The word “infiltrates” in the timeline headline is therefore stronger than the verified description of staff placements and system access.
notes: The supplied WIRED summary identifies four DOGE-affiliated NIH workers and three placements in the NIH Business System. It does not give each person's permissions, access logs, actions, or agency authorization; those records are needed to establish what access occurred and whether it was improper.

title: Trump orders Department of Education shutdown
description_short: Trump orders Department of Education shutdown
description_medium: On March 20, 2025, Donald Trump signed an executive order directing the education secretary to take steps, to the maximum extent appropriate and permitted by law, to facilitate closure of the Department of Education. The supplied account characterizes the order as an effort to effectively eliminate the department and links it to Project 2025’s influence. The materials do not detail implementation or legal responses.
description_long:
On March 20, 2025, Donald Trump signed an executive order concerning the Department of Education. The supplied account says the order directed the secretary of education, “to the maximum extent appropriate and permitted by law,” to take necessary steps to facilitate the department’s closure. It describes the intended effect as effectively eliminating the Department of Education and presents the action as an instance of Project 2025 influence on the administration.

The order’s wording, as summarized in the supplied material, is qualified by the requirement that steps be appropriate and permitted by law. That qualification is relevant: the account describes a direction to pursue closure, but does not establish that the department was actually closed or that the order itself completed that outcome. The provided facts also do not identify which department functions or programs would be affected, how statutory responsibilities would be handled, or what implementation measures followed. No court challenge, ruling, congressional response, or concrete effects on students and schools are described in the supplied material. The event records a presidential directive and its stated objective; assessing its practical reach or consequences requires further context about the order and subsequent actions.
notes: The supplied account describes an executive order directing steps toward closure only as permitted by law. It does not establish that the department closed or identify later implementation, legal challenges, or consequences. The linked TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202.

title: Trump: Labor Board rids itself of case against Elon Musk's SpaceX
description_short: Trump: Labor Board rids itself of case against Elon Musk's SpaceX
description_medium: The NLRB moved toward settlement talks in a case accusing SpaceX of firing employees who criticized Elon Musk. The April 2025 account said the case was placed on hold while negotiations began. That development changed how the labor dispute would proceed, but did not establish that a final settlement had been reached or that the allegations were disproved.
description_long: The National Labor Relations Board moved to negotiate a settlement in a case accusing SpaceX of firing workers who criticized Elon Musk. The action concerned the handling of an existing labor case. The change should be distinguished from a final dismissal or a completed settlement. Opening talks does not establish the terms of an agreement, a payment to workers or a determination that the underlying allegations were false. The linked account placed the shift in a broader context of changes to federal actions involving Musk's companies during his involvement with DOGE. That framing raises questions about enforcement priorities, but it is not proof of the motive behind this specific decision. The documented event is the pause and move toward settlement, with the allegations and unresolved outcome kept distinct.
notes: The supplied synopsis says the NLRB paused a 2022 case alleging SpaceX fired employees for criticizing Musk and began settlement talks. It gives no proposed terms, final disposition, or evidence of political direction; those details are needed to assess the title's claim that the Board abandoned the case.

title: Trump: RFK Jr. releases "health report" with fake studies
description_short: Trump: RFK Jr. releases "health report" with fake studies
description_medium: The linked timeline says the May 2025 MAHA report included citations to studies that did not exist, identifying research about direct-to-consumer drug advertising, children’s mental health and asthma medication. It reports that the report was revised after criticism and that a later review found additional citation errors. The timeline does not give the citations’ titles or the underlying verification records.
notes: The focused request to the supplied TrumpFile page returned HTTP 202 with an empty response. The synopsis names three subject areas but omits the citations and evidence used to show that studies were fictitious or misrepresented. Those records are needed for a detailed explanation of the headline's claim.
